headlines: CASH REGISTER AND 600 DOLLARS STOLEN FROM MIAMI BEACH RESTAURANT
OVERNIGHT BURGLARY AT NORMANDY DRIVE RESTAURANT SHATTERS PEACE
MIAMI BEACH OWNER DEMANDS ACTION AFTER BREAK-IN AT 7TYONE RESTAURANT
posts.article: Miami Beach police are investigating an overnight burglary after a man broke into 7tyone Restaurant on Normandy Drive. The crime took place just before 1 a.m. Friday, when a burglar smashed through the front door and took a cash register containing $600. Surveillance video captured a man wearing a hat, a backpack, and a towel over his face stepping behind the counter to grab the register. Owner Liliana Arguinzonesa arrived to find the shattered door, feeling frightened to step inside. Beyond replacing the door and lost cash, Arguinzonesa shared that the crime broke her peace. She is calling on city officials to enhance security and address dark night conditions along Normandy Drive.

headlines: DADE COUNTY OFFICIALLY BECAME MIAMI-DADE COUNTY ON NOVEMBER 13, 1997
DADE ADDED MIAMI TO ITS OFFICIAL NAME
THE ONLY COUNTY IN THE UNITED STATES WITH A HYPHENATED NAME
posts.article:
On November 13, 1997, Dade County officially changed its name to Miami-Dade County. This decision gave the region a permanent new designation and established a unique civic milestone.

Following that adjustment on November 13, 1997, Miami-Dade County earned a singular distinction across the entire nation. It is the only county in the United States with a hyphenated name. The addition of the hyphen created an official county title that remains completely unmatched anywhere else in the United States.
